title: Travessia or an account abroad?
label: Foreign account
description: Compare getting paid through Travessia and keeping money in an account abroad: costs, tax reporting, tax invoice and the path to reais.

short.title: Short answer
short.text: An account abroad holds dollars, but the money still has to come back to Brazil and be declared. Travessia receives in your client's currency and takes it to reais, with the tax invoice in the same flow.
short.note: An account abroad makes sense if you spend in dollars, for example living abroad part of the year.

rows.label: Opening
rows.us: Online, with a Brazilian CPF or CNPJ
rows.them: Often asks for a local address or ID

rows.label: Bringing it to reais
rows.us: Conversion at 0.6% and Pix in 1 business day
rows.them: International wire, with spread and fees

rows.label: Tax reporting
rows.us: Payments already in reais in the monthly report
rows.them: A foreign account goes on the annual return

items.question: Can I keep both?
items.answer: Yes. Many people use the foreign account for spending abroad and Travessia to get paid by clients.

items.question: Is the dollar balance in Travessia an account abroad?
items.answer: No. It's a foreign-currency balance inside a Brazilian account, converted when you decide.

items.question: Do I need to report anything differently?
items.answer: Payments count as income in Brazil. Check with your accountant how to report accounts you already hold abroad.
